briefTitle: Blood-brain Barrier (BBB) Opening Using Exablate Focused Ultrasound With Standard of Care Treatment of NSCLC Brain Mets

typedChecks.sourceText: Participant has a Karnofsky Performance Status ≥ 70% and/or ECOG 0-2
typedChecks.evidence_quote: Participant has a Karnofsky Performance Status ≥ 70% and/or ECOG 0-2

fuzzyCriteria.sourceText: The participant provides written informed consent for the trial
fuzzyCriteria.reasonFuzzy: Informed consent is a standard administrative requirement, not a typed clinical check.

fuzzyCriteria.sourceText: Participant is willing to comply with all study procedures for the duration of the study
fuzzyCriteria.reasonFuzzy: Willingness to comply is a subjective judgment.

fuzzyCriteria.sourceText: Participant is a NSCLC subject prescribed immune checkpoint inhibitor systemic therapy according to on-label use with the target brain lesion(s) measuring ≥ 0.5 cm in longest diameter. Target mets may include: De novo mets for which surgery and radiation can be deferred, Mets with or without history of prior radiation, Mets with history of radiation after at least 8 weeks since last radiation treatment, and In the event a previously treated met has progressed according to institutional practice within 4 weeks post radiation treatment, the met may be study eligible, and/or if in the opinion of the Investigator, the subject may benefit from the study procedure.
fuzzyCriteria.reasonFuzzy: This criterion contains multiple complex imaging and treatment conditions, including lesion measurement and investigator opinion, which cannot be expressed in a single typed check.

fuzzyCriteria.sourceText: Female subject is not planning pregnancy during the study duration and confirmed NOT PREGNANT each procedure day.
fuzzyCriteria.reasonFuzzy: Pregnancy planning and procedure-day status checks are not standard typed lab or demographic checks.

fuzzyCriteria.sourceText: Screening/Baseline laboratory values Screening/Baseline should adhere to local standard of care lab values for ICI therapy
fuzzyCriteria.reasonFuzzy: Local standard of care lab values do not provide explicit fixed numerical cutoffs in the source text.

fuzzyCriteria.sourceText: Participant has evidence of acute intracranial hemorrhage
fuzzyCriteria.reasonFuzzy: Intracranial hemorrhage presence is an imaging/clinical evaluation, not a typed brain_mets or lab check.

fuzzyCriteria.sourceText: Participant at risk for spontaneous intracranial hemorrhage (e.g., history of metastatic melanoma or other tissue histology).
fuzzyCriteria.reasonFuzzy: Risk assessment for hemorrhage is a clinical judgment.

fuzzyCriteria.sourceText: Participant has signs and symptoms of increased intracranial pressure or symptomatic mass effect, midline shift or evidence of subfalcine, uncal or tonsillar herniation.
fuzzyCriteria.reasonFuzzy: Signs and symptoms of increased intracranial pressure and mass effect are clinical/imaging judgments.

fuzzyCriteria.sourceText: Participant receiving Bevacizumab (Avastin) therapy, or other drugs with a proclivity for causing bleeding.
fuzzyCriteria.reasonFuzzy: Exclusion of drugs with a proclivity for causing bleeding is broader than a simple single-drug prior therapy exclusion.

fuzzyCriteria.sourceText: History of bleeding disorders or tissue pathologies which increase the subject's risk of hemorrhage for anticoagulation medications, implement pre-surgical standard procedure to avoid increased risk of a bleeding event.
fuzzyCriteria.reasonFuzzy: History of bleeding disorders and risk assessment involve clinical judgment.

fuzzyCriteria.sourceText: Participant has an infectious viral infection such as active Hepatitis B, Hepatitis C or detectable HIV viral load or participants with active bacterial infection such as TB (Bacillus tuberculosis) that may, in the opinion of the investigator, interfere with the subject receiving the study therapy or procedures or otherwise impact their participation in the trial.
fuzzyCriteria.reasonFuzzy: Involves investigator opinion regarding interference with the trial.

fuzzyCriteria.sourceText: Subjects with evidence of cranial or systemic infection.
fuzzyCriteria.reasonFuzzy: Evidence of cranial or systemic infection is a clinical assessment.

fuzzyCriteria.sourceText: Participant has received a solid organ or hematopoietic stem cell transplant.
fuzzyCriteria.reasonFuzzy: Prior transplant is not covered by the allowed prior therapy exclusion kinds.

fuzzyCriteria.sourceText: Participant has received a live vaccine within 28 days prior to the first on-study ICI infusion with or without Exablate.
fuzzyCriteria.reasonFuzzy: Live vaccine washout is not covered by standard typed checks.

fuzzyCriteria.sourceText: Known sensitivity to DEFINITY® ultrasound contrast agent or hypersensitivity to perflutren microsphere or its components, e.g., polyethylene glycol, as found in MiraLAX and bowel prep products.
fuzzyCriteria.reasonFuzzy: Allergy or sensitivity to contrast agents is a clinical exclusion not captured by standard typed checks.

fuzzyCriteria.sourceText: Contraindications to MRI and gadolinium-DTPA including non-MRI-compatible implanted devices, severe claustrophobia, unable to lie supine in MRI.
fuzzyCriteria.reasonFuzzy: MRI contraindications are procedural limitations.

fuzzyCriteria.sourceText: Subjects with significant liver dysfunction, (cirrhosis, hemochromatosis, severe alcohol abuse, or active hepatitis (autoimmune or infectious))
fuzzyCriteria.reasonFuzzy: Significant liver dysfunction is a clinical diagnosis rather than a strict numerical lab cutoff.

fuzzyCriteria.sourceText: Has a diagnosis of immunodeficiency or is receiving chronic systemic steroid therapy (in dosing exceeding 10 mg daily of prednisone equivalent) or any other form of immunosuppressive therapy within 7 days prior to the first on-study ICI infusion with or without Exablate. Note: prophylactic steroid use for ICI and chemotherapy infusion per institutional practice is allowed per protocol.
fuzzyCriteria.reasonFuzzy: Steroid dosing exceptions and institutional practices make this rule complex and part-dependent.

fuzzyCriteria.sourceText: Has a known additional malignancy that requires active treatment that would interfere with study procedures.
fuzzyCriteria.reasonFuzzy: Additional malignancy involving interference with study procedures requires investigator judgment.

fuzzyCriteria.sourceText: Known presence of leptomeningeal disease.
fuzzyCriteria.reasonFuzzy: Leptomeningeal disease is a specific CNS involvement not mapped to standard typed brain_mets checks.

fuzzyCriteria.sourceText: Has a diagnosis of active autoimmune disease (e.g., autoimmune Hepatitis, Guillain-Barre Syndrome, etc.) requiring systemic treatment in the past 2 years (i.e., with use of disease modifying agents, corticosteroids, or immunosuppressive drugs). Replacement therapy (e.g., thyroxine, insulin, or physiologic corticosteroid replacement therapy for adrenal or pituitary insufficiency, etc.) is not considered a form of systemic treatment. History of (non-infectious) pneumonitis that requires steroids or has current pneumonitis
fuzzyCriteria.reasonFuzzy: Active autoimmune disease and pneumonitis history involve complex clinical nuances.

fuzzyCriteria.sourceText: Has a history or current evidence of any condition, therapy, or laboratory abnormality that might confound the results of the study, interfere with the subject's participation for the full duration of the study, or is not in the best interest of the subject to participate, in the opinion of the treating investigator.
fuzzyCriteria.reasonFuzzy: Investigator discretion and potential confounding conditions are subjective.

fuzzyCriteria.sourceText: Subject is currently enrolled in another intervention based clinical trial
fuzzyCriteria.reasonFuzzy: Concurrent trial enrollment is an administrative rule.
